title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) comparing a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline to accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic task generator and validator, we selected K=200 tasks by a reproducible SHA‑256 sorting rule and evaluated a single shared generator output per task in both arms. Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair step was never invoked. All execution and scoring artifacts are archived (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4233332164d0453e2aecdb34d52a01883358d67ac30e028e6). We interpret this as a ceiling/null result under the tested model/validator/task‑selection regime and provide artifact‑grounded guidance for designing future failure‑rich evaluations.

sections.introduction: Operator intent→configuration automation promises efficiency gains but introduces risk: erroneous changes can create regressions (reachability loss, service interruption). A commonly proposed architectural mitigation is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM proposes commands, a deterministic verifier checks safety/assurance invariants, and an automated repair attempts to fix violations before apply. Although tool papers and benchmarks advocate G→V→R, causal, preregistered estimates of verifier+repair marginal utility under reproducible sampling contracts are scarce. We preregistered (cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256: a6d73a5cc0bda22e...) and executed a paired study that isolates the verifier margin by (i) using a single shared initial generator output per task and (ii) applying a deterministic validator to both arms. Our primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The run archives all provider traces, responses, and scoring JSONs to enable deterministic replay.
sections.related_work: Prior work documents LLMs for NetOps tasks, generate–validate–repair architectures, and the value of formal verification in network change planning (e.g., recent generate–validate–repair benchmarks and position papers). Surveys emphasise that operational reliability depends on surrounding machinery (retrieval, validators, guarded workflows). Our contribution is a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired causal estimate of a verifier's marginal effect on a fixed generator output—complementary to prior tool demonstrations and benchmarks that focus on pipeline feasibility or multi‑model ranking.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design. Preregistration (cand-002-gvr-loop; SHA‑256 = a6d73a5c...) fixed the paired binary design, deterministic task selection, validator coverage rule, estimands, analysis plan, seeds, and maximum model‑call budget. Task selection and sampling: a deterministic task generator produced a candidate pool; we filtered to intents covered by the preregistered deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and then selected the first K=200 tasks by ascending SHA‑256(intent_string) (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...). Model and orchestration. Requested model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Shared initial generation and arm semantics. For each task we issued exactly one shared_initial_generation call; both arms used the identical candidate_c. Baseline: candidate_c accepted and scored by deterministic validator post‑apply. Guarded: candidate_c first validated; if invalid, a single repair call (maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1) was permitted; repaired candidate revalidated. Repair calls were permitted but not mandatory. Deterministic validator. The validator parses generated text into structured field changes, enforces workflow policies (protected interfaces, must_be_down_for_fields, group minima), and returns a binary valid flag plus diagnostic traces (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, final_state). Artifact capture. We archived every provider call, response, scoring JSON, and computed SHA‑256 (execution/). Statistical analysis. Primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) produced a 95% percentile CI for the paired difference. The preregistered power calculation assumed a nontrivial baseline failure rate (~0.20); we report exact inference conditional on observed data.
sections.results: Execution and provenance. Planned episodes: 400 (two arms × 200 tasks). Completed episodes: 400. Model calls used: 200 (one shared generation per task; no repair calls invoked). All raw outputs and scoring JSONs are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4...). Primary confirmatory outcome. Complete paired counts: complete_pairs = 200. Baseline validator passes = 200/200; guarded validator passes = 200/200. Paired contingency: n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 52a0858d...). Repair invocation. The guarded repair path was never exercised: repair_applied=false in every guarded scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json). Representative diagnostics. Per‑task scoring JSONs include validator diagnostics (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, final_state snapshot). Example: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 = 3055f874...) records parsed_command_count=4 and validator.valid=true. Task difficulty metadata. Per‑task difficulty labels (task_payload.difficulty) are preserved in the task manifest and scoring JSONs. A small representative sample (tasks 000001–000006) includes difficulties {medium, hard, hard, very_hard, very_hard, very_hard}; the complete per‑task metadata for all K=200 tasks is archived under execution/scoring/*.json for deterministic aggregation by replay. Reproducibility artifacts. Full artifact fingerprints: raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4..., execution/transformation_manifest.json SHA‑256 = 79c9115584..., model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255..., and master prompt reference at provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
sections.discussion:
Statistical interpretation of the degenerate CI. When all observed pairs are concordant (here n11=200) there are no discordant pairs to drive a paired effect estimate; the exact McNemar test yields p=1.00 and the bootstrap over empirical pairs produces a degenerate percentile CI [0.00,0.00] (we executed 10,000 resamples with seed=1729 as preregistered). This is the correct descriptive inference for the observed data. However, the result is a ceiling/null outcome specific to the tested sampling and model regime and does not prove that verifiers are unnecessary in failure‑rich settings.

Why repairs were not invoked (artifact‑grounded account). Three archived facts explain the null outcome: (1) inclusion required validator coverage (we filtered to intents the validator supports), which biases the sample toward intents within validator semantics; (2) the requested model (gpt-5-mini) generated candidates that already satisfied the explicit workflow constraints encoded in the task payloads (validator.valid=true in all scoring JSONs); (3) the shared_initial_generation design fixes the generator output across arms, so repairs could only occur when the initial candidate failed validation. The run archive (execution/scoring/*.json) documents these traces and shows repair_applied=false for every guarded episode.

Design implications for future evaluator studies (artifact‑grounded guidance). To measure verifier/repair utility in confirmatory paired estimates researchers should (a) sample failure‑rich distributions (historical misconfigurations or adversarially constructed intents) rather than prefiltering by validator coverage; (b) evaluate multiple generator strengths (include weaker models) so baseline error rate > 0; (c) consider estimands that allow adaptive generator regeneration in response to validator feedback (closed‑loop), rather than the shared_initial design used here. The present artifacts contain per‑task difficulty and validator coverage flags so other researchers can deterministically construct the alternative samples and estimands from the archived JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json; execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...).

Threats to validity. Internal: shared_initial_generation prevented generator adaptation; construct: validator fidelity bounds what 'valid' means here; external: single model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic deterministic task sampling limit generality; conclusion: observed ceiling is an empirical fact under the preregistered contract, not a universal verdict on verifier utility.

Reproducibility and audit. We release the complete execution and scoring artifacts with SHA‑256 fingerprints (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6..., execution/scoring/*.json listed in the archive). Deterministic reconciliation confirms consistent episode accounting and no cross‑condition cache reuse (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). Independent auditors can replay scoring aggregates by iterating over execution/scoring/*.json files.
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered paired contract (shared_initial_generation; K=200 tasks deterministically sampled; requested_model=gpt-5-mini), we observed no difference between accepting the generator output directly and first passing it through verify→repair: baseline = 200/200 valid applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; McNemar p = 1.00; bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]. The repair path was never invoked. This ceiling/null outcome is reproducible from the archived artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...) and informs experimental design: to measure verifier value one must evaluate failure‑rich task distributions, vary generator weakness/strength, or change the estimand to permit adaptive regeneration. The run archive and validator traces are released to support deterministic replay and follow‑on studies. H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression rate under the preregistered sampling and model) was not supported by the observed data.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Synthetic deterministic task pool and the preregistered inclusion rule (validator coverage required) limit external validity to production intent distributions that contain emergent or historical misconfigurations.
Construct validity is tied to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; if the validator lacks coverage for real regression modes, the binary outcome conflates true safety with validator reach.

Design constraint: shared_initial_generation fixes generator outputs across arms and prevents generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates, not closed‑loop generator–verifier improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) rendered the preregistered power calculation inapplicable; inference is descriptive and artifact‑grounded for the tested regime.
